national_raw_news.title: 21 mins ago | National 20 PM Modi holds 15 bilateral meetings with world leaders, besides engagements with heads of interna...
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi held a series of high-level bilateral engagements on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit in New Delhi. Over the past three days, Mr Modi held 15 meetings with heads of state and government, besides several pull-aside meetings with world leaders and heads of international institutions. The meetings provided an opportunity to strengthen bilateral ties, discuss issues of mutual interest and exchange views on regional and global developments. The Prime Minister today held bilateral talks with leaders of Kazakhstan, Egypt, Indonesia and Philippines, South Africa, Burundi, Nigeria and Uganda. The Prime Minister met President of Kazakhstan Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. The two leaders reviewed cooperation in a range of areas, including politics, trade, defence and security, connectivity, energy, critical minerals, emerging technologies, the creative economy and people-to-people ties. The Prime Minister also held a meeting with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto. Mr. Modi also held talks with Philippines President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. He welcomed the Philippines’ decision to join the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure. During his meeting with South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, Mr. Modi reviewed the full range of the India-South Africa Strategic Partnership. Mr. Modi also met Nigerian Vice President Kashim Shettima. Yesterday, Mr Modi held bilateral meetings with leaders from Ethiopia, Malaysia, UAE, Vietnam and China. On Friday, the Prime Minister met leaders from Russia and Iran and also UN Secretary General.

national_raw_news.title: Lab-Grown Diamonds Offer Monumental Opportunity for India: Amit Shah 5 hours ago 54
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Amit Shah today called upon the Indian gems and jewellery industry to ensure that the entire ecosystem and manufacturing chain of lab-grown diamonds remain firmly in Indian hands. Addressing the 52nd India Gems and Jewellery Awards ceremony in Mumbai, Mr. Shah said the nature of the diamond trade is changing with the emergence of lab-grown diamonds. He said the lab-grown diamond market, in terms of volume, is expected to become nearly 50 times the size of the current diamond market, describing it as a monumental opportunity for India. The Minister said India has the infrastructure, capabilities, capital and entrepreneurial talent needed to seize this opportunity. He urged the industry to build capabilities across the entire value chain, including manufacturing machinery, diamond production, jewellery making, branding and setting up showrooms of Indian companies in cities across the world. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde and other dignitaries were present at the event. Earlier in the day, Home Minister inaugurated a specially curated exhibition of manuscripts titled “Shri Ganesh Dnyanarati” at the Asiatic Society of Mumbai. Addressing the gathering, Mr. Shah said India has a rich and vibrant knowledge tradition whose light has the potential to guide the entire world. He said this enduring legacy of knowledge has enabled the country to preserve its identity and civilisational continuity despite centuries of foreign invasions. Mr. Shah said the spirit of Bharat could never be enslaved because its memory remained alive in its history, language, culture, archives and traditions. He urged the Asiatic Society to use modern technology to take its vast repository of knowledge to people across the country. The Union Minister also visited the library and inspected the work being carried out at the Society’s manuscript conservation laboratory. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde and other dignitaries were present at the event.
